title: JEE Advanced 2026 · Paper 2
instr: Official JEE (Advanced) 2026 Paper 2 with the final answer key published by the organising IIT.
54 questions: Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, 18 in each subject, in four sections. Total 180 marks.
Section 1 – single correct option: +3 if correct, −1 if wrong, 0 if not answered.
Section 2 – one or more correct options: +4 if you choose all the correct options; +3 / +2 / +1 if you choose only some of the correct options and no wrong one; −1 if any chosen option is wrong.
Section 3 – numerical answer: +4 if correct, no negative marks. Give the value to two decimal places.
Section 4 – two question stems with two numerical questions each: +2 if correct, no negative marks.
source: JEE (Advanced) 2026 question paper and final answer key, organising IIT. Worked solutions: All in All Exam Practice.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ be two vectors, and let $P, Q$ and $R$ be the points with position vectors $\vec{a}$ , $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$, respectively, with respect to the origin $O$ . If $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}| = \sqrt{21}$ , $|\vec{a}-\vec{b}| = 3$ , and $\vec{a}$ and $(\vec{a}-\vec{b})$ are perpendicular to each other, then the area of the triangle $OPR$ is
options: $\sqrt{3}$
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}$
questions.sol:
Adding and subtracting $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=21$ and $|\vec a-\vec b|^2=9$: $|\vec a|^2+|\vec b|^2=15$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=3$.
$\vec a\perp(\vec a-\vec b)\Rightarrow |\vec a|^2=\vec a\cdot\vec b=3$, so $|\vec b|^2=12$.
Area $OPR=\tfrac12|\vec a\times(\vec a+\vec b)|=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|$.
$|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=3\cdot12-3^2=27$, so area $=\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.text: Let $T$ be the tangent to the parabola $y^2 = 16x$ at the point $(64, 32)$. Let $L$ be the tangent to the same parabola at another point $(x_1 , y_1)$ on the parabola. If $L$ and $T$ are perpendicular to each other, then the distance between the point $(x_1 , y_1)$ and the focus of the parabola, is
questions.sol:
Here $a=4$; points are $(4t^2, 8t)$. $(64,32)$ gives $t_1=4$.
Tangents at $t_1,t_2$ are perpendicular iff $t_1t_2=-1$, so $t_2=-\tfrac14$.
Point: $(x_1,y_1)=(\tfrac14,-2)$.
Focal distance $=x_1+a=\tfrac14+4=\dfrac{17}{4}$.

questions.text: Let $y : (-\infty, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ be the solution of the differential equation $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{e^{5x}y^3 + y^3}{e^x + e^x y^4},$$ satisfying $y(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. Then the value of $y(\log_e 2)$ is
options: $\sqrt{\dfrac{5+\sqrt{35}}{2}}$
$\sqrt{\dfrac{7+\sqrt{53}}{2}}$
questions.sol:
Separate: $\dfrac{1+y^4}{y^3}dy=\dfrac{e^{5x}+1}{e^x}dx=(e^{4x}+e^{-x})dx$.
Integrate: $\dfrac{y^2}{2}-\dfrac{1}{2y^2}=\dfrac{e^{4x}}{4}-e^{-x}+C$.
At $x=0$, $y^2=\tfrac12$: $\tfrac14-1=\tfrac14-1+C\Rightarrow C=0$.
At $x=\log_e2$: RHS $=4-\tfrac12=\tfrac72$, so $y^4-7y^2-1=0$.
$y^2=\dfrac{7+\sqrt{53}}{2}$, $y=\sqrt{\dfrac{7+\sqrt{53}}{2}}$.

questions.text: The value of the definite integral $$\int_0^2 \frac{1}{3^x + 3}\,dx$$ is
options: $\dfrac{\log_e 3}{3}$
$\dfrac{\log_e 3}{2}$
questions.sol:
Replace $x$ by $2-x$: $I=\int_0^2\dfrac{dx}{9/3^x+3}=\int_0^2\dfrac{3^x}{3(3^x+3)}dx$.
Add to the original: $2I=\int_0^2\dfrac{1+3^x/3}{3^x+3}dx=\int_0^2\dfrac13dx=\dfrac23$.
So $I=\dfrac13$.

questions.text:
Let $a,\ b,\ c$ be positive integers in arithmetic progression such that the equation $$ax^2 + bx + c = 0$$ has only integer solutions.

Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: $c - b$ is an integer multiple of $a$
Both the roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ are odd integers
If $c = 15$ , then $ab = 8$
If $b = 8$ , then $x = 3$ is a root of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$
questions.sol:
Integer roots give $b/a=m$, $c/a=n$ integers; AP gives $n=2m-1$, so $x^2+mx+2m-1=0$.
Discriminant $m^2-8m+4=(m-4)^2-12$ must be a perfect square $k^2$: $(m-4-k)(m-4+k)=12$ with equal parity gives $m-4=\pm4$; $m>0$ so $m=8$, $n=15$.
Equation $\equiv x^2+8x+15=0$, roots $-3,-5$; $b=8a$, $c=15a$.
(A) $c-b=7a$ ✓. (B) $-3,-5$ odd ✓. (C) $c=15\Rightarrow a=1,b=8$, $ab=8$ ✓. (D) roots are $-3,-5$, not $3$ ✗.

Let $L$ be the straight line joining the points $P(1, 2, -1)$ and $Q(2, 3, 1)$. Let $S$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $R(4, -1, 5)$ to the line $L$ . Another line passing through $R$ intersects $L$ at a point $T$ such that the point $S$ divides the line segment $PT$ internally in the ratio $|PS| : |ST| = 1 : 2$ , where $|PS|$ and $|ST|$ are the lengths of the line segments $PS$ and $ST$, respectively.

Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: The orthocentre of the triangle $PRT$ is $\left(\frac{23}{5}, -4, \frac{31}{5}\right)$
The orthocentre of the triangle $PRT$ is $(4, 3, 5)$
The area of the triangle $PRT$ is $6\sqrt{5}$
The area of the triangle $PRT$ is $18\sqrt{5}$
questions.sol:
$L$: $P+t(1,1,2)$. $(P+t\,\vec d-R)\cdot\vec d=6t-12=0\Rightarrow t=2$, $S=(3,4,3)$.
$PS:ST=1:2\Rightarrow T=P+3(S-P)=(7,8,11)$.
$RS\perp PT$: area $=\tfrac12|PT||RS|=\tfrac12\cdot6\sqrt6\cdot\sqrt{30}=18\sqrt5$.
Orthocentre lies on altitude $RS$: $H=R+\lambda(S-R)=(4-\lambda,-1+5\lambda,5-2\lambda)$.
$PH\perp RT$, $RT\parallel(1,3,2)$: $(3-\lambda)+3(5\lambda-3)+2(6-2\lambda)=6+10\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-\tfrac35$.
$H=\left(\tfrac{23}{5},-4,\tfrac{31}{5}\right)$. So (A), (D).

questions.text: Let $y = f(x)$ be the real valued function defined on the interval $(0, \infty)$ , satisfying $y(1) = 0$ and the differential equation $$x\frac{dy}{dx} = y - x^3 .$$ Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: The function $f$ has a local minimum at $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
The function $f$ has a local maximum at $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
The function $f$ is increasing in the interval $(1,\ 2)$
If $g(x) = 4x^3 - 5x^2 + \frac{3}{2}x$ for $x > 0$, then the number of elements in the set $$\{x \in (0, \infty) :\ f(x) = g(x)\}$$ is $2$
questions.sol:
$\left(\dfrac yx\right)'=\dfrac{xy'-y}{x^2}=-x\Rightarrow\dfrac yx=-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$; $y(1)=0\Rightarrow C=\tfrac12$.
$f(x)=\dfrac{x-x^3}{2}$, $f'(x)=\dfrac{1-3x^2}{2}$, $f''=-3x<0$: local max at $x=\frac1{\sqrt3}$ (B), not min.
$f'<0$ on $(1,2)$: decreasing, (C) false.
$f=g\iff \tfrac92x^3-5x^2+x=0\iff 9x^2-10x+2=0$ (for $x>0$): discriminant $28>0$, both roots positive, so 2 elements (D).

questions.text: Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of all real numbers and let $i = \sqrt{-1}$ . Consider the matrices $$S = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \text{ and } T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.$$ Let $a, b, c, d$ be real numbers such that $$ST = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}.$$ Let $$H = \{\, x + iy :\ x, y \in \mathbb{R} \text{ and } y > 0 \,\}.$$ Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: $\frac{b+ia}{d+ic} = i$
If $\omega = \frac{-1+i\sqrt{3}}{2}$ , then $\frac{a\omega+b}{c\omega+d} = \omega$
If $m$ is an integer greater than 2 such that $(ST)^2 = (ST)^m$ , then $m$ is an integer multiple of $8$
If $z \in H$ , then $\frac{az+b}{cz+d} \in H$
questions.sol:
$ST=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$: $a=0,b=-1,c=1,d=1$.
(A) $\dfrac{-1}{1+i}=\dfrac{-1+i}{2}\ne i$ — false.
(B) $\dfrac{-1}{\omega+1}=\dfrac{-1}{-\omega^2}=\omega^{-2}=\omega$ — true.
(C) $ST$ has trace 1, det 1, so $(ST)^2-ST+I=0$, $(ST)^3=-I$, order 6; $(ST)^m=(ST)^2\iff m\equiv2\pmod 6$, e.g. $m=14$ — false.
(D) $\operatorname{Im}\dfrac{-1}{z+1}=\dfrac{\operatorname{Im}z}{|z+1|^2}>0$ — true.

questions.text: Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the set of all positive integers. Consider the sets $$A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\} \text{ and } B = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\}.$$ Let $S$ be the set of all functions $f : A \to B$ such that $f(2) \neq 2$ and $f(4) \neq 4$. Consider the set $$T = \left\{ f \in S : \text{there exists a function } g : B \to \mathbb{N} \text{ such that } g\big(f(x)\big) = 2^x \text{ for all } x \in A \right\}.$$ Then the number of elements in the set $T$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$2^x$ takes distinct values on $A$, so such $g$ exists iff $f$ is one-one ($g$ can be anything off the range).
One-one $f:A\to B$: $^7P_5=2520$.
With $f(2)=2$: $^6P_4=360$; with $f(4)=4$: 360; both: $^5P_3=60$.
$|T|=2520-720+60=1860$.

questions.text: A bookshelf contains $6$ distinct books of Mathematics and $5$ distinct books of Physics. From these $11$ books, $6$ books are chosen at random. Let $X$ be the absolute value of the difference between the number of Mathematics books chosen and the number of Physics books chosen. If $\alpha$ is the mean of the random variable $X$ , then the value of $77\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
With $k$ Mathematics books, $X=|2k-6|$ and the count is $\binom6k\binom5{6-k}$, total $\binom{11}6=462$.
$k=1..6$: counts $6,75,200,150,30,1$ with $X=4,2,0,2,4,6$.
$\sum X\cdot\text{count}=24+150+0+300+120+6=600$.
$\alpha=\dfrac{600}{462}$, $77\alpha=\dfrac{600}{6}=100$.

For a real number $\alpha$ , let $[\alpha]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $\alpha$. For a finite set $S$ , let $|S|$ denote the number of elements in the set $S$ .

Consider the functions $f : (-3, 3) \to (-\infty,\ \infty)$ and $g : (-3, 3) \to (-\infty,\ \infty)$ defined by $$f(x) = [x^3]\log_e\big(1 + \sin^2(\pi(x - [x]))\big)$$ and $$g(x) = x^3 \sin^2(\pi \log_e(1 + x - [x])).$$ Let $$A = \{x \in (-3, 3) : f \text{ is discontinuous at } x\}$$ and $$B = \{x \in (-3, 3) : g \text{ is discontinuous at } x\}.$$ Then the value of $|A| + 2|B| - |A \cap B|$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\sin^2(\pi(x-[x]))=\sin^2\pi x$, so the log factor is continuous and vanishes exactly at integers.
$[x^3]$ jumps where $x^3=k$, $k=-26,\dots,26$ (53 points). At integer $x$ ($-2..2$, 5 points) the log factor is 0 and $f$ stays continuous; elsewhere it jumps. $|A|=48$.
For $g$: as $x\to n^+$, factor $\to\sin^2 0=0$ ($=g(n)$); as $x\to n^-$, $\to n^3\sin^2(\pi\log_e2)\ne0$ unless $n=0$.
$B=\{-2,-1,1,2\}$, $|B|=4$, $A\cap B=\varnothing$.
Value $=48+8-0=56$.

questions.text:
Consider the curve $C_1$ given by $$y = e^{-x} \qquad \text{for } x \in [0, 10\pi],$$ and the curve $C_2$ given by $$y = e^{-x}(\sin x + \cos x) \qquad \text{for } x \in [0, 10\pi].$$ Let $n$ be the total number of points of intersection of the curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ .

Suppose that $\alpha_1 , \alpha_2 , \ldots, \alpha_n \in [0, 10\pi]$ are the $x$ - coordinates of the points of intersection of the curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that $$\alpha_1 < \alpha_2 < \cdots < \alpha_n .$$

The value of $n$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Intersection: $\sin x+\cos x=1\iff\sin\left(x+\frac\pi4\right)=\frac1{\sqrt2}$.
So $x=2k\pi$ or $x=\frac\pi2+2k\pi$.
In $[0,10\pi]$: $x=0,2\pi,\dots,10\pi$ (6 values) and $\frac\pi2,\frac{5\pi}2,\dots,\frac{17\pi}2$ (5 values).
$n=11$.

questions.text:
Consider the curve $C_1$ given by $$y = e^{-x} \qquad \text{for } x \in [0, 10\pi],$$ and the curve $C_2$ given by $$y = e^{-x}(\sin x + \cos x) \qquad \text{for } x \in [0, 10\pi].$$ Let $n$ be the total number of points of intersection of the curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ .

Suppose that $\alpha_1 , \alpha_2 , \ldots, \alpha_n \in [0, 10\pi]$ are the $x$ - coordinates of the points of intersection of the curves $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that $$\alpha_1 < \alpha_2 < \cdots < \alpha_n .$$

Let $\beta$ be the area of the region enclosed between the curves $C_1$ , $C_2$ , and the lines $x = \alpha_1$ and $x = \alpha_4$ . Then the value of $$-\frac{1}{\pi}\log_e\left(\beta - 2\,e^{-\frac{\pi}{2}}\right)$$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\alpha_1=0,\ \alpha_2=\frac\pi2,\ \alpha_3=2\pi,\ \alpha_4=\frac{5\pi}2$.
$F(x)=e^{-x}(1-\cos x)$ satisfies $F'(x)=e^{-x}(\sin x+\cos x-1)$.
$F(0)=0,\ F(\frac\pi2)=e^{-\pi/2},\ F(2\pi)=0,\ F(\frac{5\pi}2)=e^{-5\pi/2}$; the integrand changes sign at each $\alpha_i$.
$\beta=e^{-\pi/2}+e^{-\pi/2}+e^{-5\pi/2}$, so $\beta-2e^{-\pi/2}=e^{-5\pi/2}$.
Value $=-\frac1\pi\cdot\left(-\frac{5\pi}{2}\right)=2.5$.

questions.text:
Consider the ellipses given by $$x^2 + 4y^2 = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad 4x^2 + y^2 = 1 .$$

Let $P$ be the point in the first quadrant where the given ellipses intersect. If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the tangents to the given ellipses at the point $P$, then the value of $4\tan\theta$ is ________.
questions.sol:
Subtracting: $x^2=y^2=\frac15$, $P=\left(\frac1{\sqrt5},\frac1{\sqrt5}\right)$.
Slopes: $x^2+4y^2=1\Rightarrow y'=-\frac{x}{4y}=-\frac14$; $4x^2+y^2=1\Rightarrow y'=-\frac{4x}{y}=-4$.
$\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{-\frac14+4}{1+1}\right|=\dfrac{15}{8}$.
$4\tan\theta=7.5$.

questions.stem: Question Stem for Question Nos. 17 and 18
questions.text:
Consider the ellipses given by $$x^2 + 4y^2 = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad 4x^2 + y^2 = 1 .$$

If $\alpha$ is the area of the common region that lies inside both the given ellipses, then the value of $\cot\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
By symmetry, $\alpha=8\times$ the area of the part with $0\le y\le x$; there $4x^2+y^2=1$ is the binding curve (since $4x^2+y^2-(x^2+4y^2)=3(x^2-y^2)\ge0$).
Map $4x^2+y^2=1$ to the unit circle by $u=2x$: the line $y=x$ becomes $y=u/2$, i.e. angle $\arctan\frac12$ from the $u$-axis.
Sector of the unit circle from angle $0$ to $\arctan\frac12$ has area $\frac12\arctan\frac12$; scaling back halves it: $\frac14\arctan\frac12$.
$\alpha=8\cdot\frac14\arctan\frac12=2\arctan\frac12$.
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac12}{1-\frac14}=\dfrac43$, so $\cot\alpha=0.75$.

questions.text:
A metal wire of cross-sectional area $0.5\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ and length $100\ \mathrm{m}$ is connected across a battery of e.m.f. $2\ \mathrm{V}$ and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$. The density, atomic mass and electrical conductivity of the metal are $6.35 \times 10^3\ \mathrm{kg\ m^{-3}}$, $63.5$ gm/mole and $2 \times 10^8\ \mathrm{mho\ m^{-1}}$, respectively. Assuming one conduction electron per atom of the metal, the drift velocity (in $\mathrm{mm\ s^{-1}}$) of the electrons in the wire is:
[Take Avogadro’s number as $6 \times 10^{23}$ and charge of the electron as $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C.]
questions.sol:
Wire resistance $R = \dfrac{L}{\sigma A} = \dfrac{100}{(2\times10^{8})(0.5\times10^{-6})} = 1\ \Omega$.
Current $I = \dfrac{2}{1+1} = 1\ \mathrm{A}$.
Electron density $n = \dfrac{\rho N_A}{M} = \dfrac{6.35\times10^{3}}{0.0635}\times 6\times10^{23} = 6\times10^{28}\ \mathrm{m^{-3}}$.
$v_d = \dfrac{I}{neA} = \dfrac{1}{(6\times10^{28})(1.6\times10^{-19})(0.5\times10^{-6})} = 2.08\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m/s} = 0.208\ \mathrm{mm/s}$.

questions.text: A nuclear reactor starts producing a radioactive nuclide $X$ from $t = 0$, at a constant rate of $\alpha$ per second. Each decay of $X$ produces energy $E_0$, which is utilized to heat a liquid of mass $m$ and specific heat $s$. Assuming no heat loss from the liquid and taking $\lambda$ as the decay constant of $X$, the rate of increase in the temperature of the liquid is:
options: $\dfrac{\alpha E_0}{m\,s}\left(1 - e^{-\lambda t}\right)$
$\dfrac{\alpha E_0}{m\,s}\left(e^{\lambda t} - 1\right)$
$\dfrac{\lambda E_0}{m\,s}\left(1 - e^{-\lambda t}\right)$
$\dfrac{E_0}{m\,s}\left(\alpha - \lambda e^{-\lambda t}\right)$
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = \alpha - \lambda N$ with $N(0)=0$ gives $N = \dfrac{\alpha}{\lambda}(1-e^{-\lambda t})$.
Decay rate $= \lambda N = \alpha(1-e^{-\lambda t})$, so heating power $P = \alpha E_0(1-e^{-\lambda t})$.
$m s \dfrac{dT}{dt} = P \Rightarrow \dfrac{dT}{dt} = \dfrac{\alpha E_0}{m s}(1-e^{-\lambda t})$.

questions.text: A beam of polychromatic light passes through a thin prism of prism angle $6^\circ$. The refractive index of the material of the prism varies with wavelength ($\lambda$) as $n(\lambda) = \alpha\lambda + \frac{\beta}{\lambda^2}$, where $\alpha = 3\ \mu\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and $\beta = 0.096\ \mu\mathrm{m}^2$. If $\lambda_{\min}$ is the wavelength at which the angle of minimum deviation $D_m$ is smallest, then the correct value of $D_m$ at $\lambda_{\min}$ is
questions.sol:
Thin prism: $D_m = (n-1)A$, so $D_m$ is smallest where $n$ is smallest.
$\dfrac{dn}{d\lambda} = \alpha - \dfrac{2\beta}{\lambda^3} = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda^3 = \dfrac{2(0.096)}{3} = 0.064 \Rightarrow \lambda_{\min} = 0.4\ \mu\mathrm{m}$.
$n = 3(0.4) + \dfrac{0.096}{0.16} = 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8$.
$D_m = 0.8 \times 6^\circ = 4.8^\circ$.

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$, and angular momentum $\ell$ is moving in a circular orbit of radius $r_0$ under the influence of an attractive force $\vec{F}(r) = -\frac{k}{r^2}\hat{r}$. Keeping its angular momentum unchanged, the particle is displaced radially by a small distance $\delta r \ll r_0$, due to which its radial distance varies periodically. The corresponding time period is:
options: $\dfrac{2\pi\ell^3}{mk^2}$
$2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$
$\dfrac{2\pi\ell^3}{3mk^2}$
$\dfrac{2\pi\ell^3}{5mk^2}$
questions.sol:
Circular orbit: $\dfrac{\ell^2}{m r_0^3} = \dfrac{k}{r_0^2} \Rightarrow r_0 = \dfrac{\ell^2}{mk}$.
Effective potential $U_{eff} = -\dfrac{k}{r} + \dfrac{\ell^2}{2mr^2}$; $U''_{eff}(r_0) = -\dfrac{2k}{r_0^3} + \dfrac{3\ell^2}{m r_0^4} = \dfrac{k}{r_0^3}$.
$\omega_r^2 = \dfrac{k}{m r_0^3} = \dfrac{m^2k^4}{\ell^6}$, so $\omega_r = \dfrac{mk^2}{\ell^3}$ (equal to the orbital angular frequency).
$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega_r} = \dfrac{2\pi\ell^3}{mk^2}$.

questions.text: Consider two isosceles prisms 1 and 2 with prism angles $A_1$ and $A_2$ and refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$, respectively, as shown in the figure. The faces $a_1b_1$ and $a_2b_2$ are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the mirror $M$. If a ray of light is incident on the face $a_1c_1$ and emerges from the face $a_2c_2$, then the correct statement(s) is/are:
options: If both the prisms are at minimum deviation condition, then $\frac{n_2}{n_1} = \sin\left(\frac{A_1}{2}\right) / \sin\left(\frac{A_2}{2}\right)$.
If prism 2 is at minimum deviation condition, then $\sin i_1 = n_2 \sin\left(\frac{A_2}{2}\right)$ is always true.

If both the prisms 1 and 2 are thin and are at minimum deviation condition with angles of deviation $\delta_{m1}$ and $\delta_{m2}$, respectively, then $\theta = \frac{\delta_{m1}}{2(n_1-1)} + \frac{\delta_{m2}}{2(n_2-1)}$.
If prism 1 is at minimum deviation condition, then $\sin i_2 = n_1 \sin\left(\frac{A_1}{2}\right)$ is always true.
questions.sol:
Normals to $a_1b_1$ and $a_2b_2$ are parallel to the mirror, and reflection at $M$ is symmetric, so the ray meets $a_2b_2$ with $i_2 = e_1$ always.
At minimum deviation in an isosceles prism, $\sin i = \sin e = n\sin(A/2)$.
Prism 1 at minimum deviation: $\sin i_2 = \sin e_1 = n_1\sin(A_1/2)$ — (D) true.
Prism 2 at minimum deviation: $\sin i_2 = n_2\sin(A_2/2)$, but this equals $\sin e_1$, not $\sin i_1$ in general — (B) false.
Both at minimum deviation: $n_1\sin(A_1/2) = n_2\sin(A_2/2) \Rightarrow \dfrac{n_2}{n_1} = \dfrac{\sin(A_1/2)}{\sin(A_2/2)}$ — (A) true.
The dashed lines meeting at $\theta$ are the angle bisectors from $a_1$, $a_2$, each tilted $A/2$ from the vertical faces, so $\theta = \dfrac{A_1}{2}+\dfrac{A_2}{2}$; thin prism $A = \dfrac{\delta_m}{n-1}$ gives (C) true.

questions.text: In a vacuum chamber, a particle of charge $1\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ and mass $1$ mg is projected with a velocity $(\hat{\imath} + 2\hat{\jmath})\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}$ from the $XZ$ plane at time $t = 0$ in an electric field of $1\hat{\imath}\ \mathrm{Vm^{-1}}$. At $t = 0.2$ s, the electric field is switched off and a magnetic field of $6\hat{\jmath}$ T is switched on. The acceleration due to gravity is $-10\hat{\jmath}\ \mathrm{ms^{-2}}$. Correct option(s) is/are:
options: The vertical distance of the particle from the $XZ$ plane at $t = 0.3$ s is $15$ cm.
The vertical distance of the particle from the $XZ$ plane at $t = 0.4$ s is $10$ cm.
The radius of the trajectory of the particle for $t > 0.2$ s is $20$ cm.
The particle will be in the $XZ$ plane at $t = 0.35$ s.
questions.sol:
$q/m = 10^{-6}/10^{-6} = 1$ C/kg, so $a_x = 1\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ while $E$ is on.
At $t=0.2$ s: $v_x = 1.2$ m/s, $v_y = 2 - 10(0.2) = 0$, $y = 2(0.2) - 5(0.2)^2 = 0.2$ m.
$\vec B$ is along $\hat\jmath$, so the magnetic force acts only in the $XZ$ plane: circle of radius $r = \dfrac{mv_x}{qB} = \dfrac{1.2}{6} = 0.2$ m $=20$ cm — (C) true.
Vertical motion is free fall from rest at $y=0.2$ m: $y = 0.2 - 5(t-0.2)^2$.
$t=0.3$ s: $y = 0.15$ m $=15$ cm — (A) true; $t=0.4$ s: $y=0$ — (B) false; the particle reaches the $XZ$ plane at $t=0.4$ s, not $0.35$ s — (D) false.

questions.text: Two charges $Q_1 = q$ and $Q_2 = mq$ are placed at the points $P_1(a, b)$ and $P_2\ (ma, mb)$, respectively, in the $XY$ plane, where $a, b \neq 0$ and $m \neq 0, 1$. If $V_1$ is the potential at a point in the $XY$ plane due to charge $Q_1$ and $V_2$ is the potential at that point due to charge $Q_2$. Correct statement(s) for the points at which $|V_1| = |V_2|$ is/are:
options: For $m = -1$, locus of these points is $ax + by = 0$.
For $m = 2$, the locus of these points is a circle of radius $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ centered at $\left(\frac{2}{3}a, \frac{2}{3}b\right)$
For $m = -2$, the locus of these points is a circle of radius $2\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ centered at $(2a, 2b)$
For $m = -3$, locus of these points is $3bx + 3ay = 0$.
questions.sol:
$|V_1| = |V_2| \Rightarrow r_2 = |m|\,r_1$. Write $\vec P = (a,b)$, $\vec X = (x,y)$.
$m=-1$: equidistant from $\vec P$ and $-\vec P$: perpendicular bisector through origin, $ax+by=0$ — (A) true.
$m=2$: $|\vec X-2\vec P|^2 = 4|\vec X-\vec P|^2 \Rightarrow 3X^2 - 4\vec X\cdot\vec P = 0$: centre $\tfrac23\vec P$, radius $\tfrac23|\vec P|$ — (B) true.
$m=-2$: $|\vec X+2\vec P|^2 = 4|\vec X-\vec P|^2 \Rightarrow X^2 - 4\vec X\cdot\vec P = 0$: centre $2\vec P$, radius $2|\vec P|$ — (C) true.
$m=-3$: $|m|\ne1$ gives a circle, not a line — (D) false.

questions.text: Consider an electric dipole comprising two charges $+q$ and $-q$ each with mass $m$, separated by a fixed distance $d$ and initially at rest with its dipole moment pointing along $\hat{\imath}$. A uniform electric field $E\hat{\jmath}$ is turned on at time $t = 0$ and it is turned off at $t = t_f$, when the dipole moment makes an angle $\theta_f$ with $\hat{\imath}$. Neglecting any sources of energy loss, correct option(s) is/are:
options: The center of mass of the dipole is deflected towards $\hat{\jmath}$ in the presence of the field.
If the magnitude of the final angular velocity $\omega_f = \sqrt{\frac{2qE}{md}}$, then $\theta_f = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
If $\theta_f = \pi/3$, then the change in kinetic energy of the dipole is given by $2\sqrt{3}\,qEd$.
For $\theta_f = \pi/4$, the dipole rotates around its center of mass with a constant angular velocity after $t > t_f$.
questions.keyNote: Official final key: BD or D
questions.sol:
Net force on the dipole in a uniform field is zero, so the centre of mass stays at rest — (A) false.
Work done by the field when $\vec p$ turns from $\hat\imath$ to angle $\theta_f$: $\Delta K = pE\sin\theta_f = qEd\sin\theta_f$.
For $\theta_f=\pi/3$: $\Delta K = \tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}qEd \neq 2\sqrt3\,qEd$ — (C) false.
$I_{cm} = 2m(d/2)^2 = \tfrac{md^2}{2}$; $\tfrac12 I\omega_f^2 = qEd\sin\theta_f \Rightarrow \omega_f^2 = \dfrac{4qE\sin\theta_f}{md}$.
$\omega_f^2 = \dfrac{2qE}{md} \Rightarrow \sin\theta_f = \tfrac12$, i.e. $\theta_f = \pi/6$ on the first swing — (B).
After the field is off there is no torque or force, so the dipole spins about its CM with constant $\omega$ — (D) true.

questions.text:
Ten moles of an ideal monoatomic gas, initially in state $\boldsymbol{a}$ at atmospheric pressure and temperature $T_a = 27^\circ\mathrm{C}$, is enclosed in a metal cylinder of volume $V_0$ fitted with a frictionless piston. The gas is suddenly compressed to state $\boldsymbol{b}$ with volume $V_0/3$. Now, keeping the piston stationary, the cylinder is submerged in a water bath of temperature $11^\circ\mathrm{C}$ until the gas reaches the temperature of the water bath, which is denoted as state $\boldsymbol{c}$. Finally, while still in the water bath, the piston is brought slowly to its initial position, which is denoted as state $\boldsymbol{f}$. If $R$ is universal gas constant, then the correct option(s) is/are:
[Given: $9^{1/3} = 2.08$]
options: The schematic P-V diagram of the processes described above is:
The change in internal energy in going from state $\boldsymbol{a}$ to $\boldsymbol{b}$ is $4860$R.
The net change in the internal energy in the whole process is $-240$R.
The pressure and temperature of the state $\boldsymbol{b}$ are $2.08$ times the atmospheric pressure and $624$ K, respectively.
questions.sol:
$a\to b$ adiabatic, $\gamma = 5/3$: $T_b = 300\cdot 3^{2/3} = 300\cdot 9^{1/3} = 624$ K; $P_b = P_0\,3^{5/3} = 3(2.08)P_0 = 6.24P_0$ — (D) false.
$\Delta U_{ab} = nC_v\Delta T = 10\cdot\tfrac32R\cdot 324 = 4860R$ — (B) true.
$b\to c$ isochoric cooling to 284 K, $c\to f$ isothermal expansion back to $V_0$ at 284 K, so $f$ lies below $a$ on the same vertical line, matching the sketch — (A) true.
Net $\Delta U = 10\cdot\tfrac32R(284-300) = -240R$ — (C) true.

In a single slit diffraction experiment, a slit of width $(0.016 \pm 0.002)$ mm is used to measure the wavelength of a monochromatic light source. In the diffraction pattern, the angular distance between the central maximum and first minimum is measured to be $(2^\circ \pm 40')$. The value of the fractional error in the measurement of wavelength is:
[Given: $\sin(2^\circ) = 0.035$]
questions.sol:
First minimum: $a\sin\theta = \lambda$.
$\dfrac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} = \dfrac{\Delta a}{a} + \cot\theta\,\Delta\theta$.
$\dfrac{\Delta a}{a} = \dfrac{0.002}{0.016} = 0.125$.
$\Delta\theta = 40' = \tfrac{2}{3}^\circ = 0.01164$ rad, $\cot 2^\circ \approx \dfrac{1}{0.035} \approx 28.6$, giving $\approx 0.33$.
Fractional error $\approx 0.125 + 0.33 \approx 0.46$.

questions.text: As shown in the figure, a ray $AB$ of unpolarized light enters from water of refractive index $n_w = 4/3$ into a medium of refractive index $n_p = 4/\sqrt{3}$ after passing through a glass plate of refractive index $n_g = 1.5$ and a layer of water. At a particular incident angle $i$ the reflected ray $CD$ is polarized in the direction as shown in the figure. The value of $i$ (in degrees) is:
questions.sol:
The reflected ray is plane polarized, so reflection at the water–$n_p$ interface occurs at Brewster's angle.
$\tan\theta_B = \dfrac{n_p}{n_w} = \dfrac{4/\sqrt3}{4/3} = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow \theta_B = 60^\circ$ in the upper water layer.
Across parallel layers $n\sin\theta$ is constant: $n_w\sin i = n_w\sin 60^\circ$.
Hence $i = 60^\circ$.

questions.text: As shown in the figure, the resistance of a galvanometer $G$ can be found by the half-deflection method. Here the resistance $R_2$ is adjusted such that when the key $K$ is closed the deflection in the galvanometer becomes half of the value as compared to when $K$ is open. Half-deflection is obtained at $R_2 = 4\ \Omega$ and thus the galvanometer resistance is found to be $6\ \Omega$. In this half-deflection condition the current (in mA) through the resistor $R_1$ is:
questions.sol:
$K$ open: $I_G = \dfrac{10}{R_1+6}$.
$K$ closed: $G\parallel R_2 = 2.4\ \Omega$, total $I = \dfrac{10}{R_1+2.4}$, $I_G = \dfrac{4}{10}I$.
Half deflection: $\dfrac{0.4\cdot10}{R_1+2.4} = \dfrac{0.5\cdot 10}{R_1+6} \Rightarrow R_1 = 12\ \Omega$.
Current through $R_1$ $= \dfrac{10}{14.4} = 0.694$ A $\approx 694$ mA.

questions.text: In a new system of units, the units of mass, length, time and current are $5$ kg, $5$ m, $5$ s and $5$ A, respectively. If $\mu_0$ and $\epsilon_0$ are the permeability and permittivity of free space, respectively, then in this new system of units, the magnitude of one SI unit of $\sqrt{\mu_0/\epsilon_0}$, is:
questions.sol:
$\sqrt{\mu_0/\epsilon_0}$ has the dimensions of resistance: $[M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$.
New unit $= 5\cdot5^2\cdot5^{-3}\cdot5^{-2} = 5^{-2}$ SI units $= \tfrac{1}{25}$ SI unit.
So one SI unit $= 25$ new units.

questions.text:
A container of height $2$ m, length $2$ m and breadth $1$ m is made of insulating vertical walls and two large area horizontal metal plates ($\mathrm{M_1}$ and $\mathrm{M_2}$) which extend far beyond the vertical walls in all directions. The container is partitioned into two equal chambers with a thin insulating vertical wall. The partition wall contains a small hole of cross-sectional area $\sqrt{10}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ near its bottom edge. Initially the hole is closed and the left chamber of the container is completely filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 15$ and the right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$). At time $t = 0$, the hole is opened and the liquid flows from the left chamber to the right chamber. In both the chambers, the space above the liquid has $\epsilon_r = 1$ and is maintained at atmospheric pressure. The schematic of the container at a time $t > 0$ is shown in the figure.
[Given: acceleration due to gravity is $10\ \mathrm{ms^{-2}}$.]

The height (in m) of the liquid in left chamber at $t = 500$ s is:
questions.sol:
Each chamber has base area $A = 1\ \mathrm{m^2}$; with $h_1 + h_2 = 2$, let $x = h_1 - h_2$ (initially 2 m).
Efflux speed $v = \sqrt{2gx}$; $\dot h_1 = -\dfrac{a v}{A}$, $\dot h_2 = +\dfrac{a v}{A}$, so $\dot x = -2a\sqrt{2g x}$.
$\dfrac{d\sqrt{x}}{dt} = -a\sqrt{2g} = -\sqrt{10}\times10^{-4}\sqrt{20} = -\sqrt2\times10^{-3}$ m$^{1/2}$/s.
At $t=500$ s: $\sqrt x = \sqrt2 - 0.5\sqrt2 = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2} \Rightarrow x = 0.5$ m.
$h_1 = \dfrac{2 + 0.5}{2} = 1.25$ m.

A container of height $2$ m, length $2$ m and breadth $1$ m is made of insulating vertical walls and two large area horizontal metal plates ($\mathrm{M_1}$ and $\mathrm{M_2}$) which extend far beyond the vertical walls in all directions. The container is partitioned into two equal chambers with a thin insulating vertical wall. The partition wall contains a small hole of cross-sectional area $\sqrt{10}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ near its bottom edge. Initially the hole is closed and the left chamber of the container is completely filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 15$ and the right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$). At time $t = 0$, the hole is opened and the liquid flows from the left chamber to the right chamber. In both the chambers, the space above the liquid has $\epsilon_r = 1$ and is maintained at atmospheric pressure. The schematic of the container at a time $t > 0$ is shown in the figure.
[Given: acceleration due to gravity is $10\ \mathrm{ms^{-2}}$.]

The difference in the capacitance (in F) between the metal plates at $t = 0$ and that at $t = 500$ s is $(8 - n)\epsilon_0$, where $\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space. The value of $n$ is:
questions.sol:
The region outside the container is unchanged, so only the two 1 m² chambers matter; each is a pair of series layers between plates 2 m apart.
$t=0$: left $\dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{2} = 7.5\epsilon_0$, right $\dfrac{\epsilon_0}{2} = 0.5\epsilon_0$; total $8\epsilon_0$.
$t=500$ s ($h_1 = 1.25$, $h_2 = 0.75$): left $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0}{1.25/15 + 0.75} = 1.2\epsilon_0$; right $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0}{0.75/15 + 1.25} = 0.769\epsilon_0$.
Total $\approx 1.97\epsilon_0$, difference $= (8 - 1.97)\epsilon_0 \Rightarrow n \approx 1.97$.

questions.text:
A uniform circular disk of radius $0.2$ m and mass $1$ kg is pivoted at its top point $C$ such that it can rotate freely around $C$ in the $XY$ plane, as shown in the figure. Initially, when the disk is at rest, a particle of mass $20$ g, travelling along negative $x$ direction in the $XY$ plane with speed $100\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}$, hits the circumference of the disk at a point $P$. After collision the particle moves along negative $y$ direction at a speed of $90\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}$.
[Given: the acceleration due to gravity (g) $= -\,10\,\hat{\jmath}\ \mathrm{ms^{-2}}$]

After the collision the disk starts to rotate around point $C$ in the $XY$ plane. The maximum change in the height (in m) of its center $O$ is:
questions.sol:
Take $O$ as origin: $C = (0, 0.2)$, $P = (0.2\sin45^\circ, -0.2\cos45^\circ) = (0.1414, -0.1414)$; $\vec r_{CP} = (0.1414, -0.3414)$.
Angular momentum about $C$ is conserved (pivot impulse passes through $C$).
Particle before: $L_z = 0.02[-(-0.3414)(-100)] = -0.683$; after: $L_z = 0.02[0.1414(-90)] = -0.255$ (SI units).
Disk: $I_C\omega = 0.428$, $I_C = \tfrac32MR^2 = 0.06 \Rightarrow \omega = 7.14$ rad/s, $K = \tfrac12(0.06)(7.14)^2 = 1.53$ J.
$Mg\,\Delta h = K \Rightarrow \Delta h = 1.53/10 \approx 0.15$ m.

(Assume that AgCl dissolved in water ionizes completely and that the molar conductivity of saturated AgCl solution is equal to its limiting molar conductivity.)

For strong electrolytes $\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$; $\sqrt{0.01}=0.1$, $\sqrt{0.04}=0.2$.

questions.text: The correct order of ONO bond angle in the given species is
options: $\mathrm{NO_2^+} < \mathrm{NO_2} < \mathrm{NO_3^-} < \mathrm{NO_2^-}$
$\mathrm{NO_2^-} < \mathrm{NO_3^-} < \mathrm{NO_2} < \mathrm{NO_2^+}$
$\mathrm{NO_3^-} < \mathrm{NO_2^-} < \mathrm{NO_2} < \mathrm{NO_2^+}$
$\mathrm{NO_2^-} < \mathrm{NO_3^-} < \mathrm{NO_2^+} < \mathrm{NO_2}$
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{NO_2^+}$: N has no lone electron, sp, linear → $180^\circ$.
$\mathrm{NO_2}$: one unpaired electron on N repels weakly → about $134^\circ$.
$\mathrm{NO_3^-}$: sp$^2$, trigonal planar → $120^\circ$.
$\mathrm{NO_2^-}$: a full lone pair on N compresses the angle → about $115^\circ$.

questions.text: Natural rubber on complete ozonolysis ($\mathrm{O_3}$/Zn-$\mathrm{H_2O}$) gives compound X as the major product. X gives positive iodoform and Tollen’s tests. X on heating with aqueous NaOH gives Y as the major product. Y is
questions.sol:
Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene, $[-\mathrm{CH_2C(CH_3){=}CHCH_2}-]_n$.
Cleaving every C=C gives $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_2CHO}$ (4-oxopentanal) = X: methyl ketone (iodoform +) and aldehyde (Tollens +).
In aqueous NaOH the enolate of the $\mathrm{CH_3CO}$ group attacks the CHO carbon intramolecularly, closing a five-membered ring (3-hydroxycyclopentanone).
On heating this dehydrates to the conjugated enone, cyclopent-2-en-1-one = Y → (A).

questions.text:
A known artificial sweetener X is composed of 4-chloro-4-deoxy-α-D-galactose and 1,6-dichloro-1,6-dideoxy-β-D-fructose joined by a glycosidic linkage. Structure of D-galactose is given below:
The correct structure of X is
questions.sol:
X is sucralose: an $\alpha(1\to2)\beta$ link between C-1 of the galactopyranose unit and C-2 (anomeric carbon) of the fructofuranose unit, as in sucrose.
Fructose part: C-1 and C-6 both carry Cl ($\mathrm{CH_2Cl}$), so the glycosidic O must sit on C-2 itself, not on a $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group. Options (C) and (D) link through a $\mathrm{CH_2}$–O, which would need a free C-1 OH → rejected.
Galactose part: in D-galactose the C-4 OH is axial in the $^4C_1$ chair (it differs from glucose only at C-4). So the 4-Cl must be axial.
(B) has Cl equatorial at C-4 (gluco configuration); (A) has Cl axial with an axial (α) C-1–O bond → (A).

questions.text: For a first-order reaction R ⟶ P at a given temperature, $k$ is the rate constant. For this reaction, at the given temperature, the concentrations of R and P at a time $t$ are [R] and [P], respectively. The correct graphical representation(s) for this reaction is(are)
questions.sol:
$[\mathrm R] = [\mathrm R]_0e^{-kt}$ and $[\mathrm P] = [\mathrm R]_0(1-e^{-kt})$.
(A) [P] rises with decreasing slope and levels off at $[\mathrm R]_0$; the plotted curve is concave upward → wrong.
(B) $\dfrac{d[\mathrm R]}{dt} = -k[\mathrm R]$ is a line with negative slope; the plot has positive slope → wrong.
(C) $\dfrac{d[\mathrm P]}{dt} = k[\mathrm R]_0e^{-kt}$ decays exponentially from $k[\mathrm R]_0$ → correct.
(D) $k$ is constant at fixed temperature → correct.

questions.text:
Correct statement(s) about the compounds P, Q and R is(are)
$$\underset{(1\,:\,5\ \text{ratio})}{\mathrm{Xe(g)} + \mathrm{F_2(g)}} \xrightarrow{873\ \text{K},\ 7\ \text{bar}} \mathbf{P}$$$$\mathbf{P} + \mathrm{O_2F_2} \xrightarrow{143\ \text{K}} \mathbf{Q} + \mathrm{O_2}$$$$\mathbf{Q} + \mathrm{H_2O} \xrightarrow{\text{complete hydrolysis}} \mathbf{R} + \mathrm{HF}$$
options: P has two lone pairs of electrons on the central atom.
Q has a perfect octahedral geometry.
Q can act as a fluorinating agent.
The molecular structure of R is trigonal pyramidal.
questions.sol:
Xe : F$_2$ = 1 : 5 at 873 K, 7 bar gives P = $\mathrm{XeF_4}$.
$\mathrm{XeF_4 + O_2F_2 \to XeF_6 + O_2}$, so Q = $\mathrm{XeF_6}$.
$\mathrm{XeF_6 + 3H_2O \to XeO_3 + 6HF}$, so R = $\mathrm{XeO_3}$.
(A) $\mathrm{XeF_4}$: 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, square planar → true.
(B) $\mathrm{XeF_6}$ has 6 bond pairs + 1 lone pair → distorted octahedron → false.
(C) $\mathrm{XeF_6}$ is a strong fluorinating agent → true.
(D) $\mathrm{XeO_3}$: 3 bonds + 1 lone pair → trigonal pyramidal → true.

questions.text: The correct statement(s) regarding the periodic properties of elements is(are)
options: Second ionization enthalpy of carbon atom is less than that of boron atom.
Increasing order of ionic radii: $\mathrm{Al^{3+}} < \mathrm{Mg^{2+}} < \mathrm{Na^+}$
Under identical conditions, in solid state, the density of potassium metal is more than density of sodium metal.
The H–H bond is weaker than F–F bond.
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathrm{B^+}$ is $1s^22s^2$: its 2nd IE removes an electron from a filled 2s subshell (≈2427 kJ mol$^{-1}$). $\mathrm{C^+}$ is $2s^22p^1$: the 2p electron is removed more easily (≈2353 kJ mol$^{-1}$) → true.
(B) Isoelectronic ions: higher nuclear charge gives a smaller radius, so $\mathrm{Al^{3+}} < \mathrm{Mg^{2+}} < \mathrm{Na^+}$ → true.
(C) Density of K (0.86 g cm$^{-3}$) is less than Na (0.97 g cm$^{-3}$) → false.
(D) H–H (436 kJ mol$^{-1}$) is much stronger than F–F (≈158 kJ mol$^{-1}$) → false.

questions.text:
In the following reaction sequence, P, Q, S and T are the major products.
The correct statement(s) about P, Q, S and T is(are)
options: Q on treatment with ethanol generates an aromatic aldehyde.
S gives positive phthalein dye test.
P is a dinitro compound.
T is a coloured compound.
questions.sol:
Aniline → acetanilide (protects $\mathrm{NH_2}$) → mononitration at para: P = 4-nitroacetanilide.
Hydrolysis gives 4-nitroaniline; diazotisation at 273–278 K gives Q = 4-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride.
Cumene → cumene hydroperoxide → phenol (+ acetone); Kolbe reaction then acidification gives S = salicylic acid.
Q couples with S in aqueous NaOH to give an azo dye: T is coloured → (D) true.
S has a free phenolic OH, so it gives the phthalein dye test → (B) true.
(A) Ethanol reduces $\mathrm{ArN_2^+}$ to ArH (nitrobenzene), not an aldehyde → false. (C) P is mononitro → false.

questions.text:
The correct statement(s) regarding sugars is(are)

Given: Specific rotations of L-(−)-glucose and L-(+)-fructose are −52.5° and +92.5°, respectively.
options: On treatment with $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, gluconic acid is oxidized to saccharic acid, whereas glucose is not oxidized to saccharic acid.
Fructose gives a positive Fehling’s test because it isomerises to glucose and another aldohexose in the presence of Fehling’s reagent.
Invert sugar is an equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose formed after hydrolysis of the corresponding disaccharide.
Specific rotation of invert sugar is −40°.
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ oxidises both CHO and the terminal $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ of glucose, so glucose itself gives saccharic acid → false.
(B) In alkaline Fehling’s solution fructose undergoes enediol tautomerism (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein) to glucose and mannose, which reduce $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ → true.
(C) Hydrolysis of sucrose gives equimolar D-glucose + D-fructose = invert sugar → true.
(D) D-enantiomers have opposite rotations: D-glucose $+52.5^\circ$, D-fructose $-92.5^\circ$. Equimolar mixture: $(52.5 - 92.5)/2 = -20^\circ$, not $-40^\circ$ → false.

questions.text: $\mathbf{X}^{a+}$ and $\mathbf{Y}^{b+}$ are hydrogen-like species. The wavelength of light absorbed during the transition between the states with principal quantum numbers $n = 1$ and $n = 2$ of $\mathbf{X}^{a+}$ is $\lambda$. The wavelength of light absorbed during the transition between the states with principal quantum numbers $n = 2$ and $n = 4$ of $\mathbf{Y}^{b+}$ is $9\lambda$. The lowest possible value of $(\boldsymbol{a}+\boldsymbol{b})$ is ____.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1\lambda = R_HZ^2\left(\dfrac1{n_1^2}-\dfrac1{n_2^2}\right)$.
X: $\dfrac1\lambda = R_HZ_X^2\cdot\dfrac34$. Y: $\dfrac1{9\lambda} = R_HZ_Y^2\cdot\dfrac3{16}$.
Dividing: $9 = \dfrac{4Z_X^2}{Z_Y^2}$ → $Z_Y = \dfrac{2}{3}Z_X$.
Smallest integers: $Z_X = 3$ (Li$^{2+}$), $Z_Y = 2$ (He$^+$).
For a one-electron ion the charge is $Z-1$: $a = 2$, $b = 1$, so $a+b = 3$.

questions.text: In a solvent S, a compound B is partially dissociated into C and D as given below:$$\mathbf{B} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathbf{C} + 2\mathbf{D}$$B, C and D are non-volatile in nature. The molar mass of B is 10 times the molar mass of S. The standard boiling point and the standard enthalpy of vaporization of S are 400 K and $10R$ J mol$^{-1}$, respectively ($R$ is the gas constant in J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$). A solution of B in S with an initial concentration of B as 0.25% (mass/mass) has a boiling point of 408 K at 1 bar pressure. In this solution, the mole percent of B that has been dissociated is ____.
questions.sol:
Let the molar mass of S be $M$ (kg mol$^{-1}$); B has $10M$.
$K_b = \dfrac{RT_b^2M}{\Delta_{vap}H} = \dfrac{R(400)^2M}{10R} = 16000\,M$ K kg mol$^{-1}$.
0.25 g B in 99.75 g S: $m = \dfrac{0.25\times10^{-3}/(10M)}{0.09975} = \dfrac{2.506\times10^{-4}}{M}$ mol kg$^{-1}$, so $K_bm = 4.01$ K.
$\Delta T_b = 8 = i\times4.01$ → $i \approx 1.995$.
$\mathrm{B \rightleftharpoons 2C + 2D}$: particles $= 1-\alpha+4\alpha = 1+3\alpha$ → $\alpha = \dfrac{0.995}{3} \approx 0.332$.
Mole percent dissociated ≈ 33.2%.

questions.text: Consider that the coordinating atoms of the ligands in $cis$-$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl}$ and $mer$-$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]}$ octahedral complexes are at the vertices of an octahedron. The sum of total number of the triangular faces in both the complexes having one N atom and two Cl atoms at their corners is____.
questions.sol:
A face of an octahedron uses three mutually cis vertices; a face with 2 Cl needs a cis Cl–Cl edge, and each edge belongs to exactly 2 faces.
cis-$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^+}$: one cis Cl–Cl edge → 2 faces, and the third vertex of each is N → 2.
mer-$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]}$: Cl at $+x, -x, +y$; N at $-y, \pm z$. Cis Cl–Cl edges: $(+x,+y)$ and $(-x,+y)$; each has 2 faces completed by $+z$ or $-z$ (both N) → 4.
Total $= 2 + 4 = 6$.

In the following reaction sequence, major products X and Y are acyclic monomers.
500 mol of X completely reacts with 500 mol of Y to give 1 mol of a single biodegradable acyclic copolymer Z as the only product. The amount of Z formed in grams is ____.

Given:
Atomic mass (in amu): H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, Br : 80
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{CH_3I \xrightarrow{KCN} CH_3CN \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} CH_3COOH \xrightarrow{P/Br_2} BrCH_2COOH \xrightarrow{NH_3} H_2NCH_2COOH}$: X = glycine, $M = 75$.
Caprolactam hydrolysis: Y = $\mathrm{H_2N(CH_2)_5COOH}$, $M = 131$.
Z is a single linear chain (nylon-2–nylon-6) from 1000 monomers joined by 999 amide bonds, each releasing one $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
Mass $= 500(75) + 500(131) - 999(18) = 37500 + 65500 - 17982 = 85018$ g.

questions.text:
Two volatile liquids A and B form an ideal solution. Consider a 5 molal solution of B in A inside a closed container having a total vapour pressure of 100 mm Hg at 300 K. The vapour pressure of pure A at 300K is 105 mm Hg. Assume that A and B behave as ideal gases in the vapour phase.

Given:
The gas constant $R$ = 0.08 L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
Molar mass of A is 50 g mol$^{-1}$
Molar mass of B is 57 g mol$^{-1}$
Density of liquid B at 300 K is 0.5 g/mL
1 atm = 760 mm Hg

At 300 K, the ratio of the molar volume of pure B in vapour phase to its molar volume in liquid phase is ____.
questions.sol:
5 molal: 5 mol B per 1000 g A = 20 mol A → $x_B = 5/25 = 0.2$, $x_A = 0.8$.
$100 = 0.8(105) + 0.2\,p_B^\circ$ → $p_B^\circ = 80$ mm Hg.
Vapour of pure B at its vapour pressure: $V_m = \dfrac{RT}{p} = \dfrac{0.08\times300}{80/760} = 228$ L mol$^{-1}$.
Liquid: $V_m = \dfrac{57}{0.5} = 114$ mL = 0.114 L mol$^{-1}$.
Ratio $= 228/0.114 = 2000$.

Consider the following reaction sequence in which J, K, L and M are the major products.
Given:
Atomic mass (in amu): H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, S : 32, Br : 80, Ba : 137

The volume of 1 M aqueous $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ required to completely neutralize the ammonia evolved from 5.72 g of L in Kjeldahl’s method of nitrogen estimation is ____ mL.
questions.sol:
Friedel–Crafts acylation of m-xylene at C-4 gives $\mathrm{ArCOCH_2Cl}$ (Ar = 2,4-dimethylphenyl); NaI gives $\mathrm{ArCOCH_2I}$; m-nitrophenoxide gives J = $\mathrm{ArCOCH_2OAr'}$ (Ar′ = 3-nitrophenyl).
$\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ then $\mathrm{PBr_3}$: K = $\mathrm{ArCHBrCH_2OAr'}$; check $M = 105 + 93 + 14 + 16 + 122 = 350$ ✓.
L = $\mathrm{ArCH(NH_2)CH_2OAr'}$, $M = 350 - 80 + 16 = 286$; 5.72 g = 0.020 mol.
Kjeldahl's method does not convert nitro N to $\mathrm{NH_3}$, so only the amine N counts: 0.020 mol $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
$\mathrm{2NH_3 + H_2SO_4}$: 0.010 mol $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ = 10 mL of 1 M.
